note: The security audit's rule catalogue. Documented in .claude/skills/security-rules; read by the viewer (placeholders until a rule is implemented) and by the scanner when it exists. Every ref is an official Android, Apple or Google Play page.

categories.static: Static scan of the compiled code

rules.title: Exported component without a permission
rules.why: An activity, service, receiver or provider that is exported can be started by any app. Without a permission, other apps can drive it or read its data.
rules.fix: Set android:exported="false" unless another app must reach it; otherwise guard it with a signature-level android:permission.

rules.title: Cleartext traffic allowed
rules.why: android:usesCleartextTraffic="true", or a network security config that permits cleartext, lets the app send data over HTTP, where it can be read and changed on the network. Android 17 starts deprecating the attribute.
rules.fix: Remove the attribute and use HTTPS. If one domain truly needs HTTP, allow it per domain in network_security_config.xml.

rules.title: Debuggable build
rules.why: A build with android:debuggable="true" lets anyone attach a debugger, read the app's data and run code inside its process. It must never ship.
rules.fix: Build release variants with debuggable false (Gradle's release build type does this by default) and remove the manifest attribute.

rules.title: App data can be backed up
rules.why: With android:allowBackup on (the default), backups can copy the app's data, tokens included, off the device.
rules.fix: Set allowBackup="false", or add dataExtractionRules / fullBackupContent that exclude tokens and databases.

rules.title: Hard-coded secret
rules.why: API keys, tokens, private keys or passwords compiled into the app can be read by anyone who unpacks it.
rules.fix: Keep secrets on a server. For client keys use per-user tokens, or restrict the key (package name, signing certificate, quota). Rotate any key that shipped.

rules.title: WebView native bridge
rules.why: addJavascriptInterface exposes app methods to JavaScript in the page. If the WebView loads remote or user-supplied content, that page can call them.
rules.fix: Load only trusted origins, expose as little as possible, annotate with @JavascriptInterface, or use WebMessagePort instead of a bridge.

rules.title: TLS validation switched off
rules.why: A custom X509TrustManager that accepts every certificate, or a HostnameVerifier that always returns true, disables TLS checks: anyone on the network can read and change the traffic.
rules.fix: Delete the custom checks and use the platform defaults. To trust a private certificate authority, use a network security config.

rules.title: Broken or risky cryptography
rules.why: Algorithms such as DES, RC4, ECB mode, and MD5 or SHA-1 used for security, or a fixed IV, don't protect data.
rules.fix: Use AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 with a fresh random nonce, SHA-256 or stronger, and keep keys in the Android Keystore.

rules.title: Sensitive data in logs
rules.why: Tokens, passwords or personal data written to Logcat can be read by other tools and end up in bug reports.
rules.fix: Remove the log calls, or strip them from release builds (R8 -assumenosideeffects). Never log credentials.

rules.title: Traffic readable through a user-installed CA
rules.why: While the app runs it accepts a certificate from a user-installed authority, so a proxy can read its traffic. Pinning is optional, but worth a deliberate decision for sensitive APIs.
rules.fix: Pin your API hosts' public keys: <pin-set> in the network security config on Android; the URLSession delegate or NSPinnedDomains in Info.plist on iOS.

rules.title: HTTP request seen at runtime
rules.why: A request to an http:// URL was sent while the app ran, so its data crossed the network unencrypted.
rules.fix: Serve the endpoint over HTTPS, update the client, and remove the cleartext exception that allowed it.

rules.title: Secrets stored in plain files or preferences
rules.why: After a crawl, the app's data folder holds tokens or credentials in plain files, SharedPreferences or UserDefaults. Backups and rooted or jailbroken devices can read them.
rules.fix: Keep secrets in the Android Keystore (for example EncryptedSharedPreferences) or the iOS Keychain, not in preferences or files.

rules.title: App Transport Security exceptions
rules.why: NSAppTransportSecurity exceptions (NSAllowsArbitraryLoads, per-domain exceptions) allow insecure HTTP connections.
rules.fix: Remove the exceptions and use HTTPS endpoints. Keep a per-domain exception only with a written reason.

rules.title: No privacy manifest
rules.why: An app that uses required-reason APIs, or ships SDKs on Apple's list, needs a privacy manifest (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy) declaring the data it collects and why.
rules.fix: Add PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy to the app target and update any SDK that ships its own.
